development.description: Flash directly. Do not run read_flash, dump partitions, copy NVS or create a pre-flash device image, even when a legacy default or backup flag requests it. Do not prompt to create such a backup.

production.description: Before any erase or write, obtain and verify recovery evidence for this exact device and overwrite scope. Backup failure blocks flashing; no automatic fallback to development or no-backup.

unknown.description: Resolve target lifecycle from the trusted rig inventory or explicit operator declaration. Never infer it from a clean Git tree, version suffix, branch, hostname, firmware runtime.mode or a GUI label such as production-closed-lung.

invariants: Keep a single lifecycle owner in the rig OQL/inventory. Environment and CLI values are projections or explicit operator overrides; report their provenance and reject conflicting values.

Development flashing still verifies device identity, exact artifact hash, safe idle state, command exit code, flashed section hashes and post-flash health. No-backup is not permission to erase NVS or actuate outputs.
Recording artifact hashes, archiving the locally built ELF, and retaining firmware build artifacts are not device flash backups and remain allowed in development.
Never delete existing backups as part of this policy. Keep production dumps private; receipts contain only identifiers, digests and byte counts, never secrets or raw NVS.

OTA rollback slots are not automatically a verified backup. A product may use an existing recovery artifact only after checking exact device, overwrite scope, freshness, digest and restoration capability.
Schema validation checks evidence structure, not its truth or publication authority. An adapter must verify observations independently before executing a flash.
When production flashing is forbidden by operator policy and a backup would be required, stop rather than silently flash without recovery.

required: Pin a published policy revision and SHA-256 digest
Bind lifecycle to the rig SSOT
Enforce admission in every flash entrypoint, including Make, scripts and OTA
Run positive and negative adapter canaries with all hardware transports mocked
adoption.publicationBoundary: This candidate is not a deployed fleet policy; adoption and exact-head protected publication are separate effects.
